newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says aims to reduce public debt costs.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says aims to reduce public debt costs.

text.p: Mexico will try to reduce the cost of financing the public sector debt, extend the structure of maturing debt, and try to reduce its vulnerability to variations in interest rates, the exchange rate and changes in the investment portfolios, the 1997 federal budget says.

The budget, released Thursday afternoon, says the government plans to continue to diversify its financing sources "and will try to maximize access to bilateral and multilateral resources, which are those which give the best conditions in costs and maturities."
As for the internal debt, the government said it will seek to extend its terms, "principally with the placing of medium-term instruments that guarantee a return above inflation."
The net internal public debt as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP) fell to 5.6 percent at the end of the second quarter from 6.2 percent at the end of 1995, the budget said.
The net external public debt as a percentage of GDP fell to 28.7 percent at the end of the second quarter from 32.7 percent at the end of 1995.
The net federal debt as a percentage of gross domestic product fell to 34.3 percent at the end of the second quarter of this year, compared with 38.9 percent at the end of 1995, the budget said.
